text: Link (Zelda 1 Citizens Reference). Link is the destined hero of Hyrule and the character you control. He can move in four directions and is always armed with a sword plus one other weapon of your choosing. When his sword is sheathed, he holds his shield out in front, protecting him only in the direction he faces. Link starts with three Heart Containers and can reach a maximum of 16 by the end of the game. The Blue Ring cuts received damage in half and turns Link's outfit blue. The Red Ring cuts damage down to a quarter and turns Link's outfit red. The ring color worn also affects Zelda's dress color and the shopkeepers' clothes. Underworld Overview and Second Quest Dungeon 9 Objectives. The underworld contains nine labyrinth dungeons. Some dungeon entrances, particularly the earlier ones, are right out in the open, while others require a step or two to expose. Each labyrinth has a particular shape, such as an object, symbol, or letter of the alphabet. The underworld of the second quest differs drastically from that of the first quest. Second Quest lists Dungeons 1 through 9. Dungeon 9 objectives: obtain the Red Ring, obtain the Silver Arrow, defeat Ganon, retrieve the Triforce of Power, and rescue Princess Zelda. Letter and Old Woman. The Letter is a B Button item and a key item. Show the Letter to the Old Woman, who lives in Hyrule's caves and trees, so she will sell you the Water of Life. The Water of Life is a Hyrulian recipe that restores the strength of those who drink it. Other women in Hyrule offer information about the nearby vicinity, sometimes only after being well compensated. Q: What do I need to show the Old Woman to buy the Water of Life? Legend of the Triforce: Story Background. Long ago, in the Kingdom of Hyrule, a dark army led by Ganon, a powerful warlock, seized the Triforce of Power. Princess Zelda split the Triforce of Wisdom into eight fragments and scattered them to keep them from Ganon. She sent her nursemaid Impa to find a champion. Ganon imprisoned Zelda and hunted Impa. A young lad named Link rescued Impa, who told him the story. Link vowed to save Zelda by collecting the scattered Triforce fragments and fusing them into the Triforce of Wisdom, which he needs to slay Ganon. Q: Who is Ganon and what did he seize from Hyrule? Q: How did Princess Zelda protect the Triforce of Wisdom? Q: How does Link plan to defeat Ganon?

Ganon (Boss Fight, Underworld Quest Dungeon 9). Ganon appears briefly before turning invisible and travels in small circles firing energy orbs. Stab into the space where you predict he will be; if you hit him, he appears briefly before continuing the pattern. Hitting him four times with the Magical Sword stuns him and he changes color. Then fire a Silver Arrow at him to finish him off. Defeat him and recover the Triforce of Power from Ganon's ashes. Continue to the room above, put out the fires with your sword, and rescue Princess Zelda. Q: How do I hit Ganon when he turns invisible? Gleeok and Manhandla Boss Notes. Gleeok is a recurring underworld boss, a dragon with two, three or four heads. Link must stab each attached head until it detaches and flies around the room; flying heads cannot be defeated, so dodge their projectiles and focus on attached heads. Dungeon eight of the first quest has a four-headed Gleeok, and defeating it earns a Heart Container and the final Piece of Triforce. Dungeon seven of the second quest also has a four-headed Gleeok, which yields a Heart Container and the seventh piece of the Triforce. Manhandla is a four-headed plant boss, the boss of dungeon three in the first quest. Q: How do I defeat the four-headed Gleeok boss? Q: What do I get for beating Gleeok in dungeon eight? Q: Which dungeon is Manhandla the boss of?

Level-2 Dungeon Entrance and Raft Notes. Level-2 entrance: easily found at A-1 of section 2. Approach from the area to the south. If you have the Power Bracelet, the closest Secret Passage is S4B2. Dungeon 4 preparation: obtain the Raft. Use the raft to launch off the dock at D-4 in section one and collect a Heart Container. Q: Where is the entrance to Level-2 located? Digdogger and Gohma (Boss Reference). Digdogger is a sea urchin boss with HP 8* and Damage 4, appearing as a large yellow circle with an eye in the middle. Blowing the Whistle splits it into as many as three smaller parts, which can be defeated with the Sword. It is the boss of dungeon five in the first quest and dungeon four in the second quest. Gohma is a crab monster boss with HP 2* / 6* and Damage 4 / 2. Its large central eye is its only weak spot, attacked with the Arrow. The red Gohma is defeated with one shot; the blue one takes three. Gohma is the boss of dungeon six in both quests. Q: How do I defeat Digdogger? Q: Which dungeon has the Gohma boss? Q: How many arrows does it take to beat the blue Gohma?

Zelda 1 Wiki Reference Note. The Legend of Zelda is a groundbreaking action-adventure game developed by Shigeru Miyamoto and released in Japan on February 21, 1986, for the Nintendo Famicom Disk System. It was the fourth best-selling Famicom game released in 1986, selling approximately 1,690,000 copies in its lifetime. In America it was released as a cartridge with a battery backed up memory chip that let players save progress. In the Lake Hylia coast area, pushing the upper-middle Armos reveals a shop where the fabled Blue Ring can be bought for 250 Rupees. Q: Who developed The Legend of Zelda? Underworld Overview and Second Quest Dungeon 9 Objectives. Hyrule's underworld is made up of nine labyrinth dungeons. The entrance to some dungeons, particularly the earlier ones, are right out in the open, while some require a step or two to expose. Each labyrinth is in a particular shape, be it an object, symbol, or even a letter of the alphabet. Unlike the Overworld, the underworld of the second quest differs drastically from that of the first quest. Second Quest dungeons are listed as Dungeon 1 through Dungeon 9. Dungeon 9 objectives: obtain the Red Ring, obtain the Silver Arrow, defeat Ganon, retrieve the Triforce of Power, and rescue Princess Zelda. Q: What are the objectives in Second Quest Dungeon 9? Gleeok and Manhandla Boss Notes. Gleeok is a recurring underworld boss, a dragon with two, three or four heads. Link must stab each attached head until it detaches and flies freely around the room; free heads cannot be defeated and must be dodged, so every attached head must be destroyed. Dungeon 8 of the first quest has a four-headed Gleeok, which gives a Heart Container when defeated, and the final Piece of Triforce is in the room above. Dungeon 7 of the second quest also has a four-headed Gleeok. Manhandla is a four-headed plant boss, the boss of dungeon three in the first quest, and can be defeated by one well-placed Bomb. Underworld Quest 1 Dungeon 1 and Power Bracelet Routes. Dungeon walkthrough: from the hint room, backtrack two screens, continue up twice clearing rooms for Keys, then enter room O-1 (Traps in each corner, stairwell in center). Push the left most block aside to reach the Bow; Arrows must be purchased unless already bought. Return to the map room and enter the room to the right to obtain the Compass (at Q-4). Bomb north walls in the compass room and previous room. Cross to room Q-3, defeat three Red Goriyas for the Wooden Boomerang. Room R-3 has a key but Wallmasters, which return Link to the dungeon entrance. Room R-2 holds the boss. Power Bracelet: located on Death Mountain, reached through the graveyard. Replenish health at the Fairy Fountain first, then walk west, south, and west to the Forest Maze (B1 in Section 8). Secret exit: north, west, south, west to reach the graveyard entrance (A3 in Section 8). Q: How do I get the Bow in the first dungeon? Q: Where is the Power Bracelet and how do I reach it? Q: How do I get to the graveyard from the Forest Maze?

Zelda 1 Walkthrough: Key Items, Heart Containers, and Triforce Pieces. Ganon is found in level 9, and Princess Zelda is saved by defeating him. In the 2nd Quest, the whistle reveals more Overworld secrets, including two heart containers. Obtain the White Sword from level 2 before entering level 1 if possible. Level 1 yields the Bow, the wooden boomerang, and the first Triforce piece after defeating Aquamentus. Level 2 yields the magic boomerang and the second Triforce piece after defeating Dodongo. Level 3 yields the raft and the third Triforce piece after defeating Manhandla. Level 4 yields the ladder and the fourth Triforce piece after defeating a two headed Gleeok. The Magic Sword requires at least 12 total heart containers and the movable tombstone in the upper right corner of the cemetery. Magic Shield costs 160, 130, or 90 rupees. Dungeon 4 Walkthrough Notes: Red and Blue Bubbles. This dungeon's entrance is inside the Lost Hills. Enter with at least 150 rupees; the minimum is 50 rupees to pass a room without losing a heart container. Extra rupees increase bomb capacity. Red bubbles permanently prevent drawing your sword; blue bubbles restore that ability. Touching a red bubble means finding a room with blue bubbles, such as the room one up and to the right of the entrance. From the entrance, go to the left room for a key by defeating Zols and Keeses. Enter the top door to fight a Digdogger, then the left door for Darknuts and Pol Voices to get a compass. Above, defeat Darknuts and Aquamentus to proceed. Bomb the top wall to bypass a room; never give up a heart container for 50 rupees. Push the left center block to reveal a stairway. Q: How do I get into dungeon 4 in Zelda 1? Q: What do red bubbles do in dungeon 4? Q: Where do I get the compass in the underworld quest dungeon 4?

Power Bracelet and Overworld Shops. Power Bracelet: walk three screens north, then three screens east (D4, Section 7), climb the stairs and walk one screen east (A3, Section 5) to reach the foot of Death Mountain. Push the upper-right Armos in the top row to reveal the Power Bracelet. The Power Bracelet reveals underground passageways and skips the graveyard. Lake Hylia shop (D-1, 2nd Quest) sells Blue Ring for 250 rupees and Monster Bait for 60 rupees. Medicine woman (A-1, 1st Quest) sells 2nd Potion for 68 rupees or Water of Life for 40 rupees if shown the Letter. Q: Where do I find the Power Bracelet? Q: What does the Lake Hylia shop sell and for how much? Q: How much does the medicine woman charge for Water of Life?

Zelda: Red Potion, Rupees and Key Early Items. To get a Red Potion, climb down the stairs, go one screen west, then climb up the next stairs. Place a bomb on the short horizontal part of the rock wall to meet an old woman. Use the letter, and she sells a Red Potion for 68 Rupees; keep at least 60 Rupees plus all Rupees dropped by monsters. Rupees are the currency of Hyrule: flashing rupees are worth one rupee, Blue Rupees are worth 5 Rupees, and Link can carry 255 rupees at once. Flashing hearts refill Link's life meter by one full heart. Earn 60 rupees to buy the Blue Candle. In the 2nd Quest, the whistle reveals more Overworld secrets. Gohma is a crab monster boss whose large central eye is its only weak spot, attacked with the Arrow when briefly opened. A red Gohma is defeated with one shot; a blue one takes three.
